title: Delete, then rebalance
summary: Removing a node can make an ancestor lopsided. Check the balance and rotate, done by hand.

checkpoints.text: A balanced tree: the root's left side is 2 levels and its right side 3, so its balance is -1, which is allowed.
The leaf 10 is gone. Deleting is an ordinary BST delete first; the AVL part comes next.

checkpoints.at: cout << "Its right child's balance: " << balance(root->right) << endl;
checkpoints.text: The root's left side shrank to 1 level, so its balance is 1 - 3 = -2. Its right child leans right too (-1): a right-right case, fixed by one left rotation at the root.
The left rotation lifts the root's right child.

checkpoints.at: cout << "Root balance after the rotation: " << balance(root) << endl;
checkpoints.text: 60 is the new root and its balance is 0. 50 was handed from 60 to 40, because it is between them.
60 40 20 50 70 80. After a delete, every ancestor on the way back up must be checked, and unlike insert, a delete can need more than one rotation.
